inputs.text: Albany is dressing up another restriction on lawful gun ownership as public safety. The proposal would dictate how firearms sold in New York are designed and add criminal penalties, while leaving it unclear who would face punishment. That uncertainty is no small drafting flaw: vague rules invite arbitrary enforcement and make law-abiding citizens and manufacturers vulnerable to government overreach. If lawmakers are serious about public safety, they should focus on illegal modifications—not treat responsible people as suspects. Clear laws and equal justice are foundations of public order.
